tldr: Late October brought three Show HN projects pitching a control room or control plane for LLM agents, and on Nov 4 the vLLM blog introduced Kinference, an inference control plane for vLLM on Kubernetes. On Nov 9 OpenAI described Control Room, an internal system that tracks research workloads and can stop them on safety or security concerns.
whats_new: GitSeed, posted to Hacker News on Nov 15, applies the label to coding agents: a self-hosted control plane for running AI coding agents.
why_it_matters: "Control plane" now covers four layers: agent observability, coding-agent orchestration, inference serving, and kill-switch control over research workloads. Check which layer a tool actually governs before adopting it.

status.detail: Independent projects keep using "control plane" for different layers; the newest, GitSeed, targets self-hosted coding agents.

beats.headline: Three Show HN projects pitch control surfaces for LLM agents
beats.summary: A real-time control room for agent societies, an observability and control plane for agents, and a local text-blind context control plane.

beats.headline: Kinference brings an open source control plane to vLLM on Kubernetes
beats.summary: Token rate limiting, tenant usage and cost tracking, and load balancing for scalable inference platforms.

beats.headline: OpenAI's Control Room tracks and can stop model workloads
beats.summary: Two posts on Nov 9 describe human control over AI workloads across OpenAI's research infrastructure.

beats.headline: GitSeed pitches a self-hosted control plane for coding agents
beats.summary: The label returns to open source agent tooling, this time scoped to AI coding agents.

open_questions: Does Kinference see adoption or contributions beyond its launch post on the vLLM blog?
Does OpenAI publish technical detail on how Control Room stops workloads, such as triggers or approval paths?
Do the Show HN projects (God, flightdeck, Omneum) gain users or contributors after their launch posts?
What does GitSeed actually control for coding agents: sandboxes, permissions, repo access, or just job scheduling?
Do other labs describe comparable workload tracking and stop controls?
take_for_builders: If you run vLLM on Kubernetes, evaluate Kinference for per-tenant rate limits and cost tracking in a staging cluster. Treat GitSeed and the Show HN agent tools as early experiments, and OpenAI's Control Room as a design reference you cannot deploy.
